title: Rapid single-live-cell scanning via Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) microscopy to elucidate microplastic-cell interactions
author: Friedrich, Alshareef, et al.

steps.title: Culture cell lines
steps.instruction: Maintain J774A.1 in RPMI‑1640 with 10 % FBS, 1 % sodium pyruvate, 1 % GlutaMax and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin; maintain A549 in Ham’s F12‑K with 10 % FBS and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin. Keep cultures at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Passage when confluency reaches 85–90 % (every 3–4 days).

substeps.instruction: J774A.1: detach with cell scraper, centrifuge 1000 rpm (193 rcf) 5 min, resuspend in complete medium, count using 1:1 mix with 0.4 % Trypan blue (10 µL in counting chamber), reseed at 2 × 10⁶ cells / cm² in T75 flasks.

A549: wash with 1× PBS, detach with 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA (3 mL) 5 min, quench with 7 mL complete medium, centrifuge 1000 rpm 5 min, resuspend, count as above, reseed at 1 × 10⁶ cells / cm² in T75 flasks.

steps.title: Seed cells in 6‑well plates
steps.instruction: Harvest cells from T75 flasks using the same detachment method as in step 1, determine viability with a Countess II cell counter, and proceed only if viability > 82 % for J774A.1 or > 90 % for A549. Seed J774A.1 at 5 × 10⁵ cells / well and A549 at 3 × 10⁵ cells / well in 6‑well plates. Incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Prepare microplastic suspensions
steps.instruction: Generate clean microplastic stocks, determine suitable exposure concentrations, and expose cells.

substeps.instruction: 3.1 Prepare stock suspension: sonicate commercial microplastic suspension (≈25–30 kHz) to disperse aggregates; transfer 200–400 µL to an Eppendorf tube, centrifuge 13 000 rpm 20 min, discard most supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1.5 mL PBS. Repeat the centrifugation/resuspension three times to remove surfactants. Store the final suspension in PBS. Adjust the volume of stock taken and PBS added to obtain the desired final concentration (e.g., 500 µg/mL or 1000 µg/mL). Example calculation for 10 mL of 1000 µg/mL from a 2.5 % solids stock (25 000 µg/mL): V₁ = (1000 µg/mL × 10 mL) / 25 000 µg/mL = 0.4 mL; centrifuge 0.4 mL as above, resuspend in 1 mL PBS, repeat 3×, then bring to 10 mL PBS.

3.2 Determine exposure concentration (MTT assay): seed J774A.1 at 2.5 × 10⁴ cells / well and A549 at 1 × 10⁴ cells / well in 6‑well plates with 200 µL complete medium; incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Replace medium and treat with microplastic concentrations ranging from 0–200 µg/mL for 24 h. Add 20 µL of MTT solution (5 mg/mL in PBS) per well in a dark hood, wrap plates in aluminum foil, incubate 3 h. Remove all liquid, add 200 µL DMSO, shake ~15 min, then read absorbance at 570 nm. Use a DMSO‑only well for background. Perform three independent biological replicates with technical duplicates.

3.3 Expose cells: based on MTT results select two concentrations (e.g., 25 µg/mL and 1 µg/mL). For each, take the calculated volume of the prepared PBS stock, centrifuge, and resuspend the pellet in complete medium to achieve the target concentration. Remove existing medium from the 6‑well plates (from step 2) and add 2 mL / well of the microplastic‑containing complete medium. Vortex the suspension immediately before addition to minimize aggregates. Incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Wash and detach exposed cells
steps.instruction: After the 24 h exposure, discard the microplastic suspension, wash each well three times with 1× PBS, detach cells (scraper for J774A.1, 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA for A549), collect in centrifuge tubes, centrifuge 1000 rpm (193 rcf) 5 min, remove supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 200 µL CO₂‑independent medium supplemented as follows:

substeps.instruction: J774A.1: 10 % FBS, 1 % sodium pyruvate, 1 % GlutaMax, 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin.
Adjust the final volume if necessary to obtain a suitable cell concentration for FTIR measurement.

steps.title: Assemble ZnS solid immersion device
steps.instruction: Drop‑cast 40 µL of the cell suspension onto the top 32 mm ZnS hemisphere, place the hemisphere in a humid incubator for 10–15 min to promote attachment, then position a 6 µm Mylar spacer onto the bottom ZnS hemisphere and carefully bring the two hemispheres together to sandwich the cells without disturbing them. Insert the assembled hemispheres into a lens mount, add the 3D‑printed separating ring, tighten with the retaining ring, and mount the complete device on the FTIR microscope.

steps.title: Acquire FTIR spectra
steps.instruction: Align the objective and condenser on the ZnS solid immersion device so the focus is at the centre of the dome. Record a background spectrum in an empty region (medium only) using a 40 µm × 40 µm aperture (effective ≈18 µm × 18 µm due to magnification) at 8 cm⁻¹ resolution with 512 scans. Then collect single‑cell spectra with the same aperture using 256 scans per cell. Measure approximately 20 cells per dome (up to 60 at higher cell density). Perform 4 biological replicates for A549 and 5 for J774A.1, each with 20 cells.

steps.title: Preprocess and analyze spectra
steps.instruction: In OPUS, cut each spectrum to the 3030–900 cm⁻¹ range, apply concave rubber‑band baseline correction (5 iterations, 64 baseline points), and perform vector normalization. Export the processed data and run PCA in PyChem on three spectral windows: 3000–2800 cm⁻¹, 1770–1700 cm⁻¹, and 1500–900 cm⁻¹. Use Microsoft Excel to conduct Student’s t‑tests on the PCA score plots comparing each microplastic treatment to its matched control; apply Bonferroni correction to p‑values. Baseline correction parameters were chosen to keep the biologically silent region (~2700–1800 cm⁻¹) at zero.
